content.text: For an invented two-hour outage, load 3 kW each hour, supply 1 kW in the first hour and 0 kW in the second. Unserved energy is (2+3)*1=5 kWh of 6 kWh demanded, an 83.3% share. This is not an 83.3% probability of system failure; without event probabilities there is no expected metric.

limitations: This chapter is an offline educational reconstruction, not a construction guide for high-voltage wiring, improvised fuel, unsafe heating or potentially contaminated water. The full body of human energy science extends far beyond 50 chapters.
Always keep emergency safety and public-health knowledge alongside physical equations. At a real installation, follow qualified local codes, standards and service authorities.
content.text: Take one hypothetical day with 5 kWh solar input, 3 kWh of served electricity, 1 kWh of curtailed generation, and 0.5 kWh increase of storage. The remaining 0.5 kWh must be accounted for as modeled conversion losses or an unresolved residual. Recalculate with one factor intentionally omitted and record the discrepancy. Then list the missing physical safety and supply-chain evidence rather than declaring a working microgrid.
